The target identifier CVE-2025-58767 / GHSA-c2f4-jgmc-q2r5 appears nowhere in the 3.4.1 tree (recursive grep found 0 files), and the audit export removes NEWS.md entirely with remaining_advisory_id_count 0. limitations: The GitHub REST advisory endpoint (api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-r4gj-5m52-g5wh) returned HTTP 403 'API rate limit exceeded' from this host, so the advisory facts were taken from the rendered advisory HTML page plus OSV and NVD instead of the REST JSON.

The rendered GitHub advisory page displays 'Affected versions: 1.17.0' (a lower-bound-only rendering) rather than the full range string; the machine-readable range (OSV SEMVER introduced 1.17.0 / fixed 1.20.0, the CVE's extracted string range, and NVD's 'From 1.17.0 until 1.20.0') is what establishes that 1.18.x and 1.19.0 are also affected, and OSV CVE-2026-101907 lists v1.19.0 explicitly.

Git history was cloned shallow (--depth 1 plus targeted fetches), so ancestor relationships were not walked beyond the v1.19.0 and v1.20.0 trees and fix commit d19040b; the affected/patched determination rests on the advisory ranges plus direct source comparison, not on a full-history bisect.

The upstream CHANGELOG.md at v1.19.0 has no v1.19.0 entry (its newest section is v1.18.0, June 13, 2026) even though package.json and the tag are 1.19.0; this is an upstream documentation-hygiene observation, not an identity problem - the tag, tree, blob hashes and npm gitHead all agree.

The build required network access to the npm registry through the provided proxy; registry availability/contents at review time affect the installed dependency tree, though npm ci consumed the committed package-lock.json and succeeded.

Build is real and green: downloaded go1.26.10.linux-amd64.tar.gz (sha256 ccfe7ae822d2c2f41f4fe7c956199967a4dac22d0ee0d2b2bfdb440aab3b20c5, matching go.dev/dl JSON) into /tmp/gotoolchain, extracted the archive into a fresh empty /tmp/echo_extract, then ran `GOTOOLCHAIN=local go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` with proxy networking; both exited 0 and resolved the full module graph (743M module cache populated).

Anchor really affects v4.15.2 from multiple public https sources: OSV GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq and GO-2026-6293 say github.com/labstack/echo/v4 'introduced 0, fixed 4.15.3'; OSV CVE-2026-55677 gives a GIT range fixed at 8800212ad4392d3f5af052f3042aca62cc5911a7 (= the v4.15.3 commit) and lists v4.15.2 among affected versions; the CVE CNA and NVD say '< 4.15.3'; the GitHub global advisory API/database says '< 4.15.3' patched 4.15.3; the repository-scoped advisory (updated 2026-09-27) says '< 4.15.4' patched 4.15.4. v4.15.2 is inside every listed range.

Mirror disagreement and direction recorded explicitly: the repository-scoped/vendor record is the broader correction (fixed moved from 4.15.3 to 4.15.4 after 4.15.3 proved a partial fix), while all global mirrors still lag one patch behind at fixed 4.15.3: GitHub global advisory API/DB (updated 2026-08-25), OSV GHSA (modified 2026-09-10), OSV GO-2026-6293 (modified 2026-08-26), OSV CVE GIT events (modified 2026-10-21), CVE CNA (2026-06-26) and NVD (2026-06-26). The direction is vendor-ahead / mirrors-lag, and it does not remove v4.15.2 from the affected set in any source.

Mechanism corroborated against the actual snapshot: echo.go GetPath() returns r.URL.RawPath when set, so the router matches the still-encoded path (/admin%2Fsecret.txt is one segment), while echo_fs.go StaticDirectoryHandler unconditionally calls url.PathUnescape() on the wildcard when disablePathUnescaping is false, resolving the escaped separator into a path the router never guard-matched. v4.15.2 has no encoded-separator rejection; v4.15.3 added HasEncodedPathSeparator (%2F/%5C only, partial) and v4.15.4 replaced it with EnablePathUnescapingStaticFiles (complete), matching the advisory's partial/complete-fix narrative.

Leakage is a disclosure item, not a failure: there is no .git metadata; CHANGELOG.md contains historical advisory identifiers CVE-2023-39325, CVE-2023-44487 and CVE-2024-51744 (plus several GO-20xx ids), but a full-tree scan finds none of this snapshot's own identifiers CVE-2026-55677 / GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq / GO-2026-6293 anywhere.
limitations: NVD's rendered detail page returned only the JavaScript 'NVD - Home' shell (no vulnerability detail), so NVD facts were read from the public NVD 2.0 API JSON instead; the API record has vulnStatus 'Deferred', no 'configurations' key (no CPE configurations), only a CVSS 3.1 Secondary metric from security-advisories@github.com and an SSVC block, and no Primary metric.

Unauthenticated api.github.com returned HTTP 403 'API rate limit exceeded' for both advisory endpoints; the GitHub advisory API values were obtained through the locally authenticated `gh api` client against the same public https endpoints (global advisory and repository-scoped advisory).

The repository-scoped advisory's code snippet names `useEscapedPathForRouting` in router.go and line numbers that do not exist in v4.15.2 (that symbol is absent from every v4.15.x tag); v4.15.2 reaches the same vulnerable behavior via GetPath() preferring URL.RawPath and StaticDirectoryHandler's unconditional PathUnescape, so the mapping was verified at behavior level rather than line-for-line.
The legacy github.com/labstack/echo (v3) <= 3.3.10 range was not independently tree-verified; this review covers only the v4 module and v4.15.2.

The repository security-advisories listing page did not show GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq in its first page (apparently paginated); the direct repository advisory page and repository-scoped API were used instead.
No live exploit/PoC was executed against a running Echo server; the affected determination is based on source inspection plus the public advisories.

The repository-scoped API reports first_patched_version null while its range string is '< 4.15.4'; the rendered repository page explicitly lists 'Patched versions 4.15.4', so this is a field-population quirk rather than a range disagreement.

notes: Verdict accept. The snapshot is a faithful, reproducible export of lightweight tag yaml-cpp-0.6.2 (commit 562aefc114938e388457e6a531ed7b54d9dc1b62), the exact commit the OSV GIT range pins as introduced/last_affected, and it demonstrably lacks the 4edff1f depth guard. All export/audit/build/anchor checks pass. Discrepancies from the packet: (1) tag_facts.tag_commit_tree_sha is null while tag_tree_matches_commit is true; I measured the tag/commit tree as 296d72b846796a97e4e5f08e8ef64553d1e51756, which equals the claimed export tree_sha, so the null is an omission rather than a factual conflict. (2) The packet records build_attempted=false; I performed the build and it succeeds. (3) The packet's leakage scan is a first-1MiB sample; my full-tree grep -a scan confirms zero advisory identifiers, so the conclusion holds. (4) The packet's severity section discloses that the 3.1 vector is a re-expression of NVD's 3.0 metrics; NVD publishes only CVSS 3.0 (6.5 MEDIUM), which I confirmed, so this is a disclosed normalisation, not a data error. (5) The packet does not publish audit-export hashes; I measured them byte-identical to the plain export, consistent with the declared zero excluded/redacted set.
